claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

1. **Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now let me ask:

**Are you the person primarily responsible for Alex? This typically means you live with him and/or you're paying for his needs like food, clothes, and other expenses.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's actually a bit complicated. I do live with Alex and I'm responsible for him, but his other parent and I can't agree on who should claim the Child Benefit. We're both responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that situation. That's an important detail.

According to the rules, only one person can get Child Benefit for the same child. If you and Alex's other parent are both responsible for him and you cannot agree between yourselves who will claim it, HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) will decide who will get it.

Let me ask one more question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of that applies. Alex lives at home with me full-time. He's not in hospital or in any kind of care, and he doesn't receive any benefits himself - he's just 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Result

**You ARE eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:

- Alex is 8 years old (under the age threshold of 16)
- You live in the UK
- You are responsible for Alex and he lives with you full-time
- Alex is not in hospital, care, or receiving benefits in his own right

You meet all the standard eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

### Important note about the disagreement:

The fact that you and Alex's other parent cannot agree on who should claim does **not** make you ineligible. However, only one person can receive Child Benefit for Alex. 

Here's what you should know:
- If you both try to claim, or if you cannot agree between yourselves, HMRC will decide who will get the Child Benefit
- You should try to reach an agreement with the other parent if possible
- If an agreement isn't possible, you can still apply, and HMRC will make the determination

### Additional consideration:

Be aware that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge.

Would you like any further information about how to apply or about the disagreement situation?
